source: how the ring sheet is lit and drawn (sheet.ts). Lengths in planet radii, angles in degrees. The view and phase numbers are measured on the approved hero (assets-src/saturn/code/hero_light.py) between phase 80 and 120; the last phase knot is set on the approved close.

view.note: brightness goes with ((cosine of the Sun + cosine of the view where the model was measured) / (cosine of the Sun + cosine of the view)) to a power: one for a dense sheet, one for a thin one, the ratio held between two limits

phase.note: brightness at these phase angles over the brightness where the model was measured, for a dense and a thin sheet, straight lines between and flat outside. Up to 120 degrees from the approved hero, beyond from the approved close.

shadow.note: the globe's shadow on the plane: edge half width at the limb and its growth per radius along the Sun's ray, how much farther each colour reaches into the shadow, and what is left inside it. solid: once the lens has left the hold the shaded plane lets no star through from the globe on, in the set of the kept build and in the model at every height: the space between the globe and the inner rim in the globe's shadow holds dark ring matter with no light on it, so no sky shows between the night side and the shaded rings; it grows solid between these two radii (planet radii, the globe's own radius in the plane between them). It hides the sky alone: where the view ray ends on the globe the sheet counts by its true depth (limb, graze), so the night side of the globe keeps the body's whole outline in front of it and behind it. In the light that space holds the thin sheet of dust and ice inside the rim (skim.json inner), which covers by its true depth at every height of the lens, and the ring in the light lets no star through where it holds ice (starCover: the depth of the sheet counts that many times where the view ray passes the globe; the globe shows through by the true depth)

limbNote: stars do not show through any part of the sheet that holds ice. A ray counts as ending on the globe if it passes its centre closer than the first number, and not at all beyond the second (planet radii); where it ends on the globe the sheet counts by its depth itself, by the one law of cover (skim.json handover.kept lawNote), and the globe shows through thin ice in the globe's shadow as in the hold
grazeNote: the set of the kept build can hide the globe behind the sheet where the view grazes the plane (under the first number, the sine of the angle between the view ray and the plane, the depth counts starCover times in front of the globe too; over the second the true depth counts). Both numbers lie under any sine, so that law is off, in the kept set and in the model alike: a window by the sine is a door that opens (it went out within 8 to 10 frames of the rise, since the angle at a place of the picture changes fast there). What covers the globe is the one law of cover alone (skim.json handover.kept lawNote), at every height of the lens
